title: Just a yawn
setting: A Saturday night outside a concert hall. Yuki has loved a singer for ten years and has just seen her live for the first time. Her old friend Kenta came along on her spare ticket, though he'd said he didn't know any of the songs.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: aa, sugokatta! saigo no uta, torihada tatta!
lines.ja: ああ、すごかった！最後の歌、鳥肌立った！
lines.kana: ああ、すごかった！さいごのうた、とりはだたった！
lines.english: Wow, that was amazing! The last song gave me goosebumps!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: wakaru. hora, boku mo mada torihada tatteru.
lines.ja: わかる。ほら、僕もまだ鳥肌立ってる。
lines.kana: わかる。ほら、ぼくもまだとりはだたってる。
lines.english: I know. Look, I've still got goosebumps too.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: desho? ano hito no uta, zenzen shiranai tte itteta noni.
lines.ja: でしょ？あの人の歌、全然知らないって言ってたのに。
lines.kana: でしょ？あのひとのうた、ぜんぜんしらないっていってたのに。
lines.english: Right? And you said you didn't know any of her songs.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: un, demo ii uta bakkari datta. yuki wa saisho kara naiteta ne.
lines.ja: うん、でもいい歌ばっかりだった。ユキは最初から泣いてたね。
lines.kana: うん、でもいいうたばっかりだった。ゆきはさいしょからないてたね。
lines.english: Yeah, but they were all great songs. You were crying from the very start.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: datte, juu nen matte, yatto aeta n da yo. mada jikkan wakanai.
lines.ja: だって、十年待って、やっと会えたんだよ。まだ実感湧かない。
lines.kana: だって、じゅうねんまって、やっとあえたんだよ。まだじっかんわかない。
lines.english: Well, I waited ten years, and I finally got to see her. It still hasn't sunk in.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: juu nen ka. jikkan wakanai no mo wakaru yo.
lines.ja: 十年か。実感湧かないのもわかるよ。
lines.kana: じゅうねんか。じっかんわかないのもわかるよ。
lines.english: Ten years, huh. I can see why it hasn't sunk in.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: are? kenta mo me akai yo. moshikashite, naiteta?
lines.ja: あれ？ケンタも目赤いよ。もしかして、泣いてた？
lines.kana: あれ？けんたもめあかいよ。もしかして、ないてた？
lines.english: Huh? Your eyes are red too, Kenta. Were you crying, by any chance?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: naitenai yo. chotto akubi shitara, namida deta dake.
lines.ja: 泣いてないよ。ちょっとあくびしたら、涙出ただけ。
lines.kana: ないてないよ。ちょっとあくびしたら、なみだでただけ。
lines.english: I wasn't crying. I yawned, and my eyes watered, that's all.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: saigo no uta de akubi? tsumaranakatta tte koto?
lines.ja: 最後の歌であくび？つまらなかったってこと？
lines.kana: さいごのうたであくび？つまらなかったってこと？
lines.english: A yawn, during the last song? So you were bored?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: chigau chigau! nanka wakannai kedo, kyuu ni namida dete kita n da yo.
lines.ja: 違う違う！なんかわかんないけど、急に涙出てきたんだよ。
lines.kana: ちがうちがう！なんかわかんないけど、きゅうになみだでてきたんだよ。
lines.english: No, no! I don't know why, but the tears just suddenly came.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sore, naita tte iu n da yo.
lines.ja: それ、泣いたって言うんだよ。
lines.kana: それ、ないたっていうんだよ。

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: wakatta yo. honne iu to, boku mo chotto naita.
lines.ja: わかったよ。本音言うと、僕もちょっと泣いた。
lines.kana: わかったよ。ほんねいうと、ぼくもちょっとないた。
lines.english: Fine. If I'm honest, I cried a bit too.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: yappari! kenta made naku hodo yokatta n da ne.
lines.ja: やっぱり！ケンタまで泣くほどよかったんだね。
lines.kana: やっぱり！けんたまでなくほどよかったんだね。
lines.english: I knew it! So it was good enough to make even you cry.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: un, honto ni yokatta. yuki wa? sukoshi wa jikkan waite kita?
lines.ja: うん、ほんとによかった。ユキは？少しは実感湧いてきた？
lines.kana: うん、ほんとによかった。ゆきは？すこしはじっかんわいてきた？
lines.english: Yeah, it was really good. What about you? Has it started to sink in?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un, yatto waite kita. a, dame, mata namida desou.
lines.ja: うん、やっと湧いてきた。あ、だめ、また涙出そう。
lines.kana: うん、やっとわいてきた。あ、だめ、またなみだでそう。
lines.english: Yeah, it's finally sinking in. Oh no, I'm going to tear up again.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: yamete yo. boku mo mata torihada tatte kita.
lines.ja: やめてよ。僕もまた鳥肌立ってきた。
lines.kana: やめてよ。ぼくもまたとりはだたってきた。
lines.english: Don't. Now I've got goosebumps again too.

choices.english: Kenta yawned through the last song because he didn't know it, and Yuki is upset that he found it boring.
Kenta blames a yawn for his teary eyes, but he ends up admitting the concert made him cry a little.
Kenta says he didn't cry, and Yuki believes him, since he didn't know any of the songs.

questions.explanation: Lines 7-8: Yuki sees that Kenta's eyes are red too and asks if he was crying. He says no, he just yawned and his eyes watered (akubi shitara, namida deta dake). In line 9 she asks if that means he was bored, and in line 10 he says no, the tears just suddenly came (kyuu ni namida dete kita). Yuki tells him that's called crying (line 11), and in line 12 he admits it: honne iu to, boku mo chotto naita. A is wrong: the yawn was only Kenta's excuse. He says chigau chigau! (line 10), and that the concert was really good (line 14). C is wrong: Yuki doesn't believe him (line 11), and he ends up admitting he cried.

questions.english: After lunch at the office, you give a big yawn and your eyes water. Mai, at the next desk, looks over and asks, "e, naiteru no? daijoubu?" Tell her you're not crying: your eyes just watered when you yawned.
questions.kana: え、ないてるの？だいじょうぶ？
questions.answer: Say you're not crying (naitenai yo), and that your eyes only watered because you yawned, with namida ga deru in the past: akubi shitara namida deta dake. In casual speech ga usually drops.

modelAnswers.romaji: naitenai yo. akubi shitara, namida deta dake.
modelAnswers.ja: 泣いてないよ。あくびしたら、涙出ただけ。
modelAnswers.english: I'm not crying. I yawned and my eyes watered, that's all.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, chigau chigau. akubi shitara, namida dete kichatta.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、違う違う。あくびしたら、涙出てきちゃった。
modelAnswers.english: No, no, that's not it. I yawned, and my eyes started watering.

questions.explanation: Kenta uses it to deny crying: akubi shitara, namida deta dake (line 8). Then he gives himself away with kyuu ni namida dete kita (line 10, the tears just started coming), and at the end Yuki says mata namida desou (line 15, I'm going to tear up again). namida ga deru is tears coming out on their own: from a yawn, onions or laughing, or when something moves you. naku is crying from emotion. That's why Mai asks naiteru no?, and why Yuki tells Kenta sore, naita tte iu n da yo (line 11): tears because a song moved you count as crying. A yawn doesn't, so say naitenai and namida deta dake. With a friend like Mai, casual is right, and ga usually drops.

questions.english: Right after the concert, what does Yuki say about the last song?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、最後の歌について何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、さいごのうたについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, saigo no uta ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: I got goosebumps from the last song! (morau: get, as in being given something)
Goosebumps came out at the last song! (deru: come out, as tears do)
The last song gave me goosebumps!

questions.explanation: Line 1: 'saigo no uta, torihada tatta!' In Japanese, goosebumps stand up: torihada ga tatsu, and in casual speech ga usually drops. Kenta uses it twice: hora, boku mo mada torihada tatteru (line 2, look, I've still got goosebumps too) and boku mo mata torihada tatte kita (line 16). A is wrong: morau is 'get' as in being given something, so torihada moratta copies English 'got goosebumps' word for word. B is wrong: deru is the verb for tears (namida deta, line 8), but goosebumps don't come out, they stand up. Each reaction keeps its own verb: namida ga deru, torihada ga tatsu.

questions.english: You've just passed an exam you studied for all year. Your manager, Tanaka-san, comes over and says, "shiken, ukatta sou desu ne. omedetou gozaimasu." Thank him, and say it still hasn't sunk in.
questions.ja: 試験、受かったそうですね。おめでとうございます。
questions.kana: しけん、うかったそうですね。おめでとうございます。
questions.romaji: shiken, ukatta sou desu ne. omedetou gozaimasu.
questions.answer: Thank him (arigatou gozaimasu), then say it hasn't sunk in yet with jikkan ga waku in the negative: mada jikkan ga wakanai desu. With your manager, keep ga and add desu. With friends it's just mada jikkan wakanai.

modelAnswers.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu. demo, mada jikkan ga wakanai desu.
modelAnswers.ja: ありがとうございます。でも、まだ実感が湧かないです。
modelAnswers.english: Thank you. It still hasn't sunk in, though.

modelAnswers.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu. jitsu wa, mada zenzen jikkan ga wakanai n desu.
modelAnswers.ja: ありがとうございます。実は、まだ全然実感が湧かないんです。
modelAnswers.english: Thank you. Honestly, it hasn't sunk in at all yet.

questions.explanation: After finally seeing the singer, Yuki says mada jikkan wakanai (line 5, it still hasn't sunk in). Kenta answers jikkan wakanai no mo wakaru yo (line 6), and later asks sukoshi wa jikkan waite kita? (line 14, has it started to sink in?). jikkan is the real feel of something, and waku is a feeling welling up, so it's mostly said in the negative after big news like passing an exam, a new job or a baby. Don't say mada wakaranai or rikai shite nai, which sound as if you don't understand the news. Listen for one n: wakanai (doesn't well up, from waku) against wakannai (I don't get it), which Kenta says in line 10 (nanka wakannai kedo). With your manager, keep ga and add desu: mada jikkan ga wakanai desu.
